summary: The shared toolbox for the hand-built charts, imported by the area chart, histogram, sparklines, risk line and world map. It provides unique ids for SVG definitions, the `niceMax` axis rounding and the `linear` scale, the Fritsch–Carlson `monotonePath` curve, the `responsive` ResizeObserver wrapper that redraws a chart when its width changes, the edge-fading gridline mask, and helpers that turn CSS colour tokens into real colours.

notes.text: Header comment listing what the module offers. Keeping these helpers in one place means each chart file only has to describe its own drawing.

`counter` is module-level state shared by every chart, and `uid(prefix)` increments it before use to return ids like `area-1` or `spark-7`. Gradients, masks and clip paths are referenced with `url(#id)` and ids are global to the whole page, so two charts reusing one id would pick up each other's definitions.
JSDoc and signature for `niceMax`, which rounds an axis maximum up to a **nice** number: 1, 2, 2.5 or 5 times a power of ten. A top gridline labelled 500 is far easier to read than one labelled 437.
Guard: zero or a negative value returns 1, because the logarithm on the next line is undefined there and an axis still needs a positive height.
`exp` is the power of ten at or just below the value, i.e. its order of magnitude: `Math.log10(437)` is about 2.64, `Math.floor` makes it 2, and 10 raised to the power 2 gives 100.

Picks the first multiplier in `[1, 2, 2.5, 5, 10]` that reaches the value: for 437, 100, 200 and 250 are too small and 500 fits, so `niceMax(437)` returns 500. The trailing 10 guarantees a match, since the value is always below ten times `exp`.

`linear` builds a linear scale. It is curried (a function that returns a function): give it a data domain `d0..d1` and a pixel range `r0..r1`, and it returns `v => r0 + (v - d0) / (d1 - d0) * (r1 - r0)`, which maps values proportionally. Passing the range bottom-first flips the axis so bigger values go up, and `|| 1` avoids dividing by zero when the domain is a single point.

JSDoc and signature for `monotonePath(points)`, which turns `[x, y]` pixel points into an SVG path string using Fritsch–Carlson monotone cubic interpolation. The curve is smooth but **monotone** between neighbouring points, so unlike ordinary smoothing it never bulges above a peak or below a dip, i.e. it never invents values that aren't in the data.
Edge cases: no points gives an empty path, and a single point gives just a move command `M x,y` because there is nothing to connect.
Working arrays: `dx` holds each segment's width, `slope` each segment's straight-line gradient (its secant), and `tangent` the slope the curve will have as it passes through each point.
For each segment between point i and i + 1, stores its width and its secant slope (rise over run); `dx[i] || 1` protects against two points sharing an x.
The two end points have only one neighbouring segment, so their tangents copy that segment's slope.

Interior tangents: when the slopes on either side have opposite signs or one is zero (their product is at most 0), the point is a peak, a valley or the edge of a flat stretch, so its tangent is 0 and the curve is level there instead of sailing past it. Otherwise the tangent is the average of the two neighbouring slopes.

Second pass, the Fritsch–Carlson correction, one segment at a time. A flat segment (slope 0) forces both of its tangents to 0, so the curve stays perfectly level between equal values; `continue` moves on to the next segment.

`a` and `b` are the segment's two end tangents divided by its own slope, and `s = a² + b²`. If `s > 9` the pair lies outside a circle of radius 3, the region where the cubic could overshoot, so both tangents are scaled by `k = 3 / √s` back onto that circle, which guarantees the segment stays monotone (**no overshoot**).
Starts the path string with a move to the first point.

For each segment, appends a cubic Bézier command `C cp1 cp2 end`. Both control points sit a third of the way across the segment (`h = dx / 3`) and are shifted by `h × tangent`, so the curve leaves and enters each point with exactly the computed slope: the standard conversion of a cubic Hermite segment (end points plus slopes) into Bézier form.
Returns the finished string for a path's `d` attribute; the closing brace ends `monotonePath`.

JSDoc and signature for `responsive(el, draw)`: it calls `draw(width, first)` now and again whenever the container's width changes. SVG charts are drawn at fixed pixel sizes, so they must be redrawn to fit a new layout.
Closure state: `width` is the last width drawn, and `first` stays true until the first draw has happened.

`run` measures the element's width in whole pixels and bails out if it is 0 (hidden or not laid out yet) or unchanged. The unchanged check ignores the observer's initial notification and height-only changes (drawing the chart changes the element's height), so the chart is redrawn only on a real width change; an extra redraw would replace the SVG and cut its entrance animation short.
Records the width and calls the chart's `draw` with it and the `first` flag (charts animate only on their very first draw, not on every resize), then clears the flag.
A `ResizeObserver` calls `run` whenever the element changes size: window resizes, the sidebar collapsing, panels reflowing.

Draws immediately rather than waiting for the observer. ResizeObserver notifications are delivered during the browser's rendering step, which hidden or background tabs never run, while reading `clientWidth` forces layout synchronously, so the chart exists even if the page loads in a background tab.
Returns a cleanup function that stops observing; pages register it (`ctx.add`, see main.js) so it runs when the user navigates away. The closing brace ends `responsive`.

`fadeMask(id, w, h)` returns SVG definitions: a horizontal white gradient whose opacity rises from 0 to 1 over the first 8% of the width, stays at 1 until 92%, then falls back to 0, plus a `mask` holding a full-size rect painted with it. In an SVG mask, opaque white shows content and transparent hides it, so gridlines drawn under this mask dissolve at the left and right ends instead of stopping abruptly.

SVG presentation attributes such as `fill` or `stop-color` don't reliably accept `var(--token)`, and canvas `fillStyle` never does, so colours are resolved first. `cssVar(name)` reads a custom property's computed value from the root element (`--low` becomes `#8a9bb0`), and `trim()` strips any surrounding whitespace.

`resolveColor` accepts a token name or a literal colour: anything starting with `--` is looked up with `cssVar`, anything else (like `#fff`) passes straight through. The optional chaining `?.` lets a missing colour return `undefined` instead of throwing.

`LEVEL_COLORS()` maps each risk level to its real colour from tokens.css. It is a function rather than a constant, so the colours are read from CSS each time a chart draws instead of being frozen when the module is imported.
